directAnswer: To set up push notifications, you need to implement a service worker and configure your web application to request user permission for notifications.
summary: This guide outlines the steps to set up push notifications for web applications, including platform-specific instructions and common pitfalls.

sections.heading: Understanding Push Notifications
sections.body: Push notifications allow web applications to send messages to users even when the app is not open. This requires a service worker and user consent.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Setup
sections.body: The setup process may vary slightly depending on the platform or framework you are using.

steps.title: Register a Service Worker
steps.detail: In your JavaScript file, register a service worker using navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js'). Ensure the service worker file is correctly set up to handle push events.

steps.title: Request User Permission
steps.detail: Use Notification.requestPermission() to prompt the user for permission to send notifications. Handle the user's response accordingly.

steps.title: Subscribe to Push Notifications
steps.detail: Once permission is granted, use the PushManager to subscribe the user to push notifications. This typically involves calling pushManager.subscribe with appropriate options.

steps.title: Send Notifications
steps.detail: Use your server to send push notifications to subscribed users. Ensure you have the correct endpoint and authentication in place.

faqs.question: What browsers support push notifications?
faqs.answer: Most modern browsers, including Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, support push notifications, but ensure to check compatibility for specific features.

faqs.question: Can users opt-out of push notifications?
faqs.answer: Yes, users can manage their notification preferences in their browser settings and opt-out at any time.

faqs.question: Are there any limits to push notifications?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are limits on the number of notifications that can be sent in a given time frame, and excessive notifications can lead to users disabling them.

caveats: Service workers must be served over HTTPS, except for localhost.
User permission for notifications is required and can be revoked at any time.
